description: Convert cups, tablespoons, teaspoons, fluid ounces, pints, quarts, gallons, milliliters, and liters. Ten converters, one per pair, each with its own table and worked examples.
intro: Every recipe measures volume, and no two recipes use the same units. An American recipe says cups. A European recipe says milliliters. A drinks recipe says fluid ounces, a soup recipe says quarts, and a brine recipe says gallons. The volume is the same. Only the words change.

Each converter below handles one pair of units, both ways. Type cups and get tablespoons, or type tablespoons and get cups back. The table underneath shows the common amounts at a glance, and the worked example shows the maths, so the page answers the question even before you touch the converter.

All ten converters use US customary definitions, the system American recipes are written in. Where the metric or imperial version differs, the page says so, because a metric cup is not a US cup and an imperial pint is not an American pint.
